name: Corporate & Conference Hosting
short: Plenaries, summits and leadership forums that stay on time and on message.
need: A full-day agenda, senior speakers, sponsors to acknowledge, and a room that drifts after lunch.
role: I anchor the programme from opening to close: framing each session, introducing speakers properly and managing time without making it visible.
contributes: Run-of-show review and timing notes before the day
Speaker introductions written from real bios, with names and titles checked
Transitions that carry your theme from one session to the next
Calm recovery when slides, microphones or speakers run late
outcome: A programme that feels deliberate, with every speaker set up to land their message.

name: Master of Ceremonies
short: Galas, awards and launches with energy, warmth and a firm hand on the clock.
need: An evening with many moving parts: awards, performances, dinner service, VIP remarks, and one chance to get it right.
role: I carry the show. I set the tone, build anticipation, keep the pace and make every winner and guest feel the moment is theirs.
contributes: Script and cue sheet worked through with your producer
Protocol, names and titles confirmed in advance
Energy pitched to the room: celebratory, never noise for its own sake
Live adjustments when the running order changes
outcome: An event your guests talk about afterwards, for the right reasons.

name: Moderation & Facilitation
short: Panels and executive conversations that sound like real conversations.
need: Expert panellists, a short slot and an audience that wants substance, not four speeches in a row.
role: I prepare the conversation with the panel, ask the follow-up the audience is thinking, balance the voices and bring it to a clear close.
contributes: Briefing calls or notes with each panellist
A question plan built around your objectives
Fair airtime, and gentle control of dominant voices
Audience Q&A kept on topic
outcome: Clear takeaways for the audience, and panellists who feel looked after.

name: Entertainment & Brand Experiences
short: Activations, showcases and festivals that need real stage presence.
need: A brand moment where the audience chose to be there, and can leave whenever they like.
role: I bring late-night television energy and theatre timing to hold the audience, and land your message in my own voice.
contributes: Audience interaction that feels spontaneous because it was planned
Brand messages delivered naturally, not read off a card
Smooth hand-offs to performers, DJs and guests
Reading the crowd: when to lift the room and when to let it breathe
outcome: Energy that holds, and a message people actually hear.

name: Broadcast & Interview Hosting
need: A presenter for a branded series, a webcast, a hybrid event or a long-form interview.
role: I bring studio discipline to your production: tight links, researched interviews and ease with cameras, cues and talkback.
contributes: On-camera presenting and script input
Interview research and question development
Live-stream and hybrid-event presenting
Voice-over
outcome: Content that sounds broadcast-ready the first time.
note: Availability depends on the project and my broadcasting commitments, and is subject to employer policy.

name: Speaking & Creative
short: Talks on storytelling and communication; creative direction and scripting.
need: A speaker who talks about communication from practice, or a creative lead for a production.
role: Drawing on broadcast and theatre, I speak on storytelling, effective communication, youth engagement and creative leadership, and take on selected creative direction, scripting and music direction.
contributes: Keynotes and workshop sessions
Script and story development
Creative direction for stage and live productions
Music direction and arrangement
outcome: A session or production shaped by someone who has done the work, on air and on stage.
